title: Count Good Nodes in Binary Tree
summary: Count nodes whose value is at least as large as every value on their root-to-node path.
statement: Count nodes whose value is at least as large as every value on their root-to-node path. Equal values qualify. The root always counts.

examples.explanation: The root, 4, and 5 qualify. Node 5 is counted despite its smaller parent.
The equal child qualifies and the smaller child does not.
The root is the only node.

hints: Conceptual: A large value on one branch does not affect nodes on another branch.
Directional: Carry the largest value seen on the current path with each pending node.
Implementation: Count a node when it reaches or exceeds the carried maximum, then pass the updated maximum to both children.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary space for iterative depth-first traversal, where h is the height.
